Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test calls StringUtils.newStringUtf8(null) and expects a null return rather than a NullPointerException (NPE). The test also calls StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(null) with the same expectation. The bug report description confirms that these newStringXXX methods should return null on null input, but this behaviour might have been lost after a certain commit (related to CODEC-136).

Examining the code, the newStringUtf8 method simply delegates to newString(byte[], Charset) with Charset.UTF_8. The newString method implements a null check: if the input byte array is null, it returns null; otherwise, it returns a new String constructed from the bytes and charset.

This means newStringUtf8(null) should return null as expected, so the method appears to be correctly handling null inputs.

However, the test also calls newStringIso8859_1(null) which is likely similar but is not shown yet. If newStringIso8859_1 does not perform the null check and directly constructs a new String from the null byte array, it would cause a NullPointerException.

The issue report indicates that this null handling capability was lost for multiple similar newStringXXX methods. The current code snippets confirm that newStringUtf8 correctly delegates to newString, which does the null check. The missing null handling in other newStringXXX methods such as newStringIso8859_1 is the suspected cause of the NPE.

Thus, the bug likely arises because some newStringXXX methods (like newStringIso8859_1) do not delegate to newString or do not implement the null check themselves, causing a NullPointerException when called with null instead of returning null.

To confirm, inspection of the newStringIso8859_1 method implementation is needed to verify whether it calls newString or directly constructs new String bytes ignoring null checks.

This diagnosis fits both the test failure (expecting null but getting NPE) and the issue description about the null input handling regressions after switching to Charset-based construction methods.

Next, get the code snippet for the method StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(byte[]) to verify.

messages.content: "338 :     public static String newStringIso8859_1(final byte[] bytes) {\n339 :         return new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1);\n340 :     }"

The implementation of newStringIso8859_1(byte[]) creates a new String directly from bytes and Charsets.ISO_8859_1 without checking if bytes is null.

This explains the test failure and the bug report's description: when null is passed to newStringIso8859_1(null), it immediately calls new String(null, charset), causing a NullPointerException instead of returning null.

In contrast, newStringUtf8(byte[]) calls newString(byte[], Charset), which has the null check and returns null if bytes is null, preventing NPE.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that newStringIso8859_1 (and possibly other newStringXXX methods) do not implement the null input check and do not delegate to newString(byte[], Charset) which does. This omission leads to NPE when null inputs are given.

Fixing these methods to either delegate to newString(byte[], Charset) or implement a null check themselves will restore the expected null-return behaviour for null inputs and prevent NullPointerExceptions.

This aligns with the bug report that these methods stopped returning null on null input after switching to using Charset objects.

Summary:
- newStringUtf8 handles null input correctly by delegating to newString which returns null on null bytes.
- newStringIso8859_1 does not do the null check, causes NPE on null input.
- The bug is missing null input handling in some newStringXXX methods.

The best fix would be to modify all newStringXXX methods to delegate to newString(byte[], Charset) similarly to newStringUtf8.
